eyebrow: A short, repeatable list of root causes

steps.label: A legacy ACL grants access to AllUsers / Everyone
steps.sub: easy to set by accident, easy to miss — it's not where most engineers look

steps.label: A policy is set public "temporarily"
steps.sub: for a static site or shared download, then never reverted

steps.label: Nobody is watching for drift
steps.sub: a private setting flipped later goes unnoticed without continuous monitoring

eyebrow: S3 Block Public Access — overrides ACLs and policies
code:
# Four settings, account-level or bucket-level:
#   BlockPublicAcls        - new public ACLs rejected
#   IgnorePublicAcls       - existing public ACLs ignored
#   BlockPublicPolicy      - new public bucket policies rejected
#   RestrictPublicBuckets  - existing public policies ignored

# Enabled account-wide: no bucket owner can make a
# bucket public by accident, regardless of its own settings.
caption: The single highest-leverage control against this entire class of incident.

code:
# Storage account level:
#   "Allow Blob public access" = Disabled
#   -> makes every container's own setting inert

# Per-container public access level:
#   Private    - no anonymous access
#   Blob       - anonymous read of blob data only
#   Container  - anonymous read + listing (most dangerous)
caption: Azure Policy can enforce the account-level setting across an entire subscription.

steps.label: Private endpoints / VPC endpoints
steps.sub: route traffic entirely off the public internet, enforceable via policy

steps.label: AWS Config / Azure Policy, continuously
steps.sub: catch a setting drifting back toward public, not just at deploy time

steps.label: Encryption never substitutes for access control
steps.sub: a public ACL on an encrypted object is still a publicly readable object
